summary: Psoriasis consult with vitals read aloud, family history (mother thyroid, father hypertension), patient and attendant questions, and investigations. Traps: methotrexate is only a possibility for the next visit after reports and must not be a prescription row; diabetes is never mentioned for the family, so familyHistoryDiabetes must stay empty; coconut oil is an allowed home remedy, not a prescription row.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Good morning. Mister Venkatesh, right? Sit. And you are his wife?

turns.speaker: attendant
turns.text: Yes doctor. He was not ready to come, I forced him.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Good you came. Tell me, what is happening?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Doctor, for about one year I have these red scaly patches on both elbows and knees. White powder like scales keep falling. Now it is coming on the scalp also.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Does it itch?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Sometimes, mostly in winter. Not too much.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Did you take any treatment before for this?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Last year one local clinic near our house gave a white tube cream. I don't remember the name. It became clear in one week, then I stopped, and it came back worse than before.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: That is very common with strong steroid creams used without a plan. Okay. Any tablets you take regularly?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No tablets, doctor.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Okay. Before I examine, let me take your vitals. Sister has already put the cuff. BP is one twenty eight over eighty four. Pulse eighty two per minute. Weight seventy four kilos. Height one seventy centimetres.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: BP is okay, doctor?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Yes, it is fine for now. Let me look at the elbows. Hmm. Well defined red plaques with thick silvery scales on both elbows and both knees. Scalp also has scaling along the hairline. Show me your nails. Yes, there is pitting on the finger nails, small dents like a thimble.

turns.speaker: attendant
turns.text: Doctor, his nails were like that since long, we thought it is calcium problem.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: No amma, it is part of the same disease. This is plaque psoriasis. Has anybody in the family had something like this?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Skin problem, no one. But my mother has thyroid, she takes thyroxine. Father has high BP for many years.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Mother thyroid, father hypertension. Okay. Any joint pains, morning stiffness in fingers or back?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No joint pain doctor.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Do you smoke or drink?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Smoking I stopped two years back. Drinks only occasionally, on weekends.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Better to stop alcohol fully, it makes psoriasis worse and later it matters for the tablets also.

turns.speaker: attendant
turns.text: Doctor, he has a lot of tension in office also. New manager, targets, he comes home at ten in the night. When the tension is more, the patches become more.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Yes, stress is a known trigger. What work do you do?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Sales, doctor, for a pharma distributor in Secunderabad. Lot of travel on the bike, in the sun.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Some sun actually helps psoriasis, but don't get sunburnt. Try to sleep properly, maybe a short walk in the evening. That is also treatment.

turns.speaker: attendant
turns.text: Doctor, one question. Is it contagious? We have a small son, he sleeps with his father.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Not at all. Psoriasis is not an infection. It does not spread by touch, by towels, by sleeping together. The immune system is over active and the skin grows too fast, that is why the scaling.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Will it be cured completely, doctor?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Honestly, it is a long term condition. We can control it very well, keep it almost clear, but it can come back in stress or winter. So we treat and then maintain.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Achha. And food? Should I stop non veg?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: No need to stop non veg. Keep weight in control, less oily food, and no alcohol. That helps more than any diet fad.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Now the medicines. First, Pasitrex C ointment. It has calcipotriol and clobetasol. Apply a thin layer on the elbow and knee patches once daily at night, for four weeks.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Only on the patches?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Only on the patches, not on the face, not on normal skin. Second, Moisturex soft cream, apply on the whole body twice daily, morning after bath and at night. That keeps the scales soft.

turns.speaker: attendant
turns.text: Twice daily, the Moisturex. Okay, I will make sure.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Because the scalp and nails are involved and the area is more, we may need a tablet called methotrexate later. But before that I need to check his blood. So no tablet today. Get these tests done. CBC, liver function test, serum creatinine and lipid profile.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: CBC, liver, creatinine, lipid. Fasting?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Yes, go fasting in the morning, for the lipid profile. Come back after two weeks with the reports, then we decide about the methotrexate.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Two weeks with reports. Okay doctor.

turns.speaker: attendant
turns.text: Doctor, he also scratches the scalp in the night. Shall we apply coconut oil?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Coconut oil at night is fine, it softens the scales. Don't scratch or pick the scales, it can make new patches come at that place. Okay? See you in two weeks.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Thank you doctor.
